source.title: Emergent Semantic Role Understanding in Language Models

record.file_problem: None noted; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports QA-SRL downstream performance across model scales, an application relevant to V6, but does not measure the claimed pretraining-loss laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. as background but does not measure held-out cross-entropy against parameters, tokens, or compute; fit scaling exponents; test extrapolation; or study compute-optimal allocations. Its own relevant results are QA-SRL F1 across scales. Neuron ablations, CKA, and other mechanistic results do not measure any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study trains four GPT-style models (0.4M–56.7M transformer parameters) on one corpus, WikiText-103. It reports QA-SRL downstream F1 at each scale under frozen-probe and full fine-tuning conditions. That is a scale-versus-downstream-performance result in a new setting, so it bears on V6. It is weak evidence: only four points, no fitted or predictive relation, no loss-to-task mapping, and data held fixed. No result bears on V1–V5 or V7; Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only as background and to justify a fixed tokenizer.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that semantic role information is decodable from frozen pretrained representations at all scales, 12–19 F1 above an architecture-matched random baseline. Frozen probes improve with scale but do not match full fine-tuning, and the gap widens, so emergence is partial. Role representations shift from concentrated to distributed as scale grows, with Agent neurons going from causal to interfering. They draw no conclusions about loss scaling laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains custom GPT-style models across four sizes and measures QA-SRL F1, frozen probes, and fine-tuning; it does not reproduce the original loss-fitting or compute-allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported QA-SRL F1 differs by model scale and training condition (random baseline, frozen probe, full fine-tuning); best probe layer also changes with scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Role-selective neuron ablation effects change sign with scale: Agent neurons are causal in small models and interfering in larger ones, across custom, GPT-2 and Pythia. Separately, the number of components needed for 80% of causal importance grows with scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Internal mechanisms for a fixed capability become more distributed with model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: A normalized emergence score (frozen gain over random, relative to the full-fine-tuning gain) falls with scale, from 0.60 to 0.47. Fine-tuning's added contribution grows from 8.2 to 21.1 F1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The share of downstream performance available from frozen pretrained representations shrinks with scale as fine-tuning gains grow.

record.code_released: Code and trained models with checkpoint weights are available from the authors upon request.
record.problems: The downstream evidence is limited to QA-SRL and custom models with 0.4M–56.7M transformer parameters; no predictive fit or extrapolation is reported. The paper notes WikiText-103 has approximately 103 million tokens and the Medium model is underconverged. Custom-model neuron-ablation results are single-seed point estimates, though those ablations are not evidence on the listed scaling-law versions.
record.rows_left_out: Neuron-ablation, CKA, and representation-visualization results (Sections 4.3–4.5 and Appendices C–H) were omitted because they do not measure any listed claim version. Table 13 best-layer probe results are included separately from Table 2 QA-SRL results.

untested.parts: No predictive fit or functional form for F1 versus scale, no extrapolation, and no link between downstream F1 and pretraining loss. Only one task (QA-SRL), and data and compute are not varied independently of parameters.
Held-out pretraining loss is never reported against parameters, tokens or compute.
No compute-optimal allocation is studied; the Chinchilla ratio is cited only as a limitation.
Depth and width co-vary with size; there is no fixed-parameter shape comparison.

missing.what: Frozen-embedding (SEP-only) pretrained F1 rises with scale: 23.9, 27.9, 30.5, 31.6. The gain over random is significant only at Base and Medium.
Frozen GPT-2 best-layer QA-SRL probe F1: Small 31.2% versus Medium 35.1%. This is a second family showing a downstream increase with scale.
Pre-training trajectory: per-layer probe F1 stabilises within 10–20 epochs and steady-state F1 grows monotonically with scale.

record.verdict_notes: V6 evidence is thin: four model sizes, a fixed 103M-token corpus (so larger models are data-limited), one task, and no fit. The random-baseline rows are controls and should not be linked to V6. The Table 13 best-layer values are post hoc per-scale maxima and come from 500-sample probes.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and range.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Loss sensitivity to depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes.

The study reports QA-SRL F1 at four custom model scales, but does not fit a predictive relationship, test extrapolation, compare downstream performance with pretraining loss, or examine other downstream tasks.
Dependence of scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices, and bending of loss curves.

relationships.condition: Custom decoder-only models trained on WikiText-103, QA-SRL F1, four scales 0.4M–56.7M, frozen probe and full fine-tuning
relationships.reason: F1 rises monotonically with scale: frozen 36.4 to 44.7, full fine-tuning 44.6 to 65.8, best-layer pure probe 17.2 to 30.8. This shows improvement with scale only, not a predictive law.
relationships.display_finding: F1 increased monotonically from 36.4→44.7 for frozen probes, 44.6→65.8 for full fine-tuning and 17.2→30.8 for best-layer pure probes, without testing a predictive law.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Custom WikiText-103 models on QA-SRL at the four reported parameter scales; frozen probes, full fine-tuning, and best-layer pretraining probes
reader_labels.reason: QA-SRL F1 rises across the reported scales in the frozen and fully fine-tuned conditions, and best-layer probe F1 also rises across scales (rows V6-T2-Tiny-Frozen through V6-T2-Medium-Frozen, V6-T2-Tiny-Full through V6-T2-Medium-Full, and V6-AppI-Tiny through V6-AppI-Medium). This supports a scale-associated downstream improvement in this setting, but does not establish a predictive law.
